definition: LPA* or Lifelong Planning A* is an incremental heuristic search algorithm based on A*.
details: It was first described by Sven Koenig and Maxim Likhachev in 2001.

explainer.lead: LPA* (Lifelong Planning A*) is an incremental heuristic search algorithm based on A*. It matters because it reuses prior search results when the problem changes, instead of starting over.

tiers.eli5: Like re-planning a route after a road closes by reusing the map work you already did.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply LPA* in dynamic path planning, repairing the search tree as edge costs change rather than recomputing. A pitfall is that frequent or far-reaching changes erode the savings over fresh search.
tiers.paperLevel: An incremental heuristic search algorithm based on A*, first described by Sven Koenig and Maxim Likhachev in 2001; it reuses previous search information across successive problem instances.

explainer.example: A robot reroutes through a changing environment by updating its LPA* search rather than running A* from scratch.
